items.evidence: play --ticks N --inputs ... --set board=2|3 --settings FOLDER printed one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball{x,y,z}, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds (plus an extra 'phase'). The board option only takes effect after a 0:enter in the script (see defects).
README frame command (--ticks 200 --set board=3 --inputs 0:enter --frame readme.png --size 800x480) and my own frames: every PNG has a valid signature and an 800x480 header.

sounds/*.wav, and the same files rewritten by '--ticks 0 --sounds snd': mono 16-bit 48 kHz; coin 0.35 s, bounce 0.25 s, fall 0.9 s, clear 0.8 s; peak 0.48 to 0.89; different hashes and very different zero-crossing rates (216, 477, 1375, 2483 per second).

Tick 1 is title with selected Start. menu_down,menu_down,menu_up,menu_up gave Settings, Quit, Settings, Start. 0:enter gave screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3 and texts 'Board 1 of 3','Score: 0','Lives: 3'.

Settings first shows 'Volume: 8','Language: English'. Four menu_right gave 9, 10, 10, 10 and menu_left gave 9; twelve menu_left clamped at 0. On Language, menu_right gave es and menu_left gave en. Back plus enter returned to the title.

Language es: title Empezar/Ajustes/Salir; settings Ajustes/Volumen: 8/Idioma: Espanol/Volver; play 'Tablero 2 de 3','Puntos: 0','Vidas: 3'; paused En pausa/Continuar/Salir al titulo; won Ganaste/Puntos: 30/Pulsa Enter...; lost Fin del juego/Puntos: 10/Pulsa Enter... No English text was left (the name Roll aside).

A run with --settings set1 set volume 9 and es. The next run with set1 started at volume 9, es and Spanish texts, and a later run started at 0 and en after those were set. A run without --settings started at volume 8, en.
Board 1 with no input: y first <=0.3 at about tick 29 (0.2475), rose back to 0.49, bounced again, and rested at y 0.24993 from tick ~60 to 650. Sounds: bounce x2.

From rest, a push at 80 that ends at 110: right gave x 0.515 at 110, then 1.01, 1.51 and 2.16 at 125, 140 and 160. Left, up and down gave the mirror results in -x, -z and +z. The ball kept moving after the push ended until it left the edge.

My 13-input script took the board 1 coins: each coin added 10 to the score, left 'coins' and added 'coin' to sounds. On the 4th coin (tick 694): board 2, 'clear' added, ball at (-3,1.248,0) on the board 2 start, 3 board 2 coins, 6 crates at x=0, z -0.5/0/0.5, y 0.25/0.75.
--set board=2, 0:enter, no input: at ticks 100, 301 and 600 every crate was within 0.001 of its place (y 0.2499/0.7493).

Board 2 with right held from tick 80: the ball bounced off the wall at x -0.6 and then pushed the middle column, so 2 crates were at x 0.57 (tick 300), 1.58 (tick 400) and 2.92 (tick 500). The ball reached x=1 at about tick 395, against about tick 164 on an empty floor. No crate y went below 0.249.

I could not push a crate off an edge in 5 scripts: an x=0 lane, a z=-0.5 lane, a z=-0.45 lane, a re-strike after a fall, and a +z push on the z=0.5 column. Each time the ball slipped round the crates and fell. Crates got only as far as x 3.23 or z 0.8, so I never saw a crate fall or leave 'crates'.

Board 1, right push: coin (2,0) taken, then a fall gave lives 2, 'fall' in sounds and the ball back at (0,1.24,0), with 3 coins (the taken one stayed taken). I cleared board 1 later in that run, and board 2 began with lives 2. On board 2 a fall left the crates unchanged (3.23, 0.25, 0.1 kept).
--set board=3, 0:enter, no input: bridge_x was 1, 2, 1, 0 at ticks 90, 180, 270, 360, and again 1, 2, 0 at 450, 540, 720.

Inputs 258:right,288:none,366:left,394:none left the ball nearly still on the bridge. From tick 720 to 900, x went -0.18 to 1.99 while bridge_x went 0 to 2 (|x-bx| <=0.18), and it rode until 1200 without falling. With a right push at 100 to 130 the ball left the slab at tick ~205 while bridge_x was 1.7. It fell into the gap and lives went to 2.

--set board=3 --inputs 0:enter,258:right,288:none,366:left,384:none: screen won at tick 645, score 30, sounds ...coin,coin,clear. The state was identical at ticks 660, 690 and 699, with a right push at 660 included. Enter at 700 gave the title.
Board 2, 3 falls: screen lost, lives 0. From tick 750 to 849 score, ball, coins and crates were unchanged, with right and left pushes at 780 and 830. Enter at 850 gave the title.

Board 3, escape at 100: paused with Resume selected. Ball and bridge_x were identical at ticks 101, 150 and 199, and on board 2 the crates were identical from 11 to 300. Enter (Resume) at 200 resumed. Escape, menu_down to Quit_to_title and enter gave the title.
Two runs of board 2 strike-and-fall scripts (600 ticks, and 1300 ticks with --at) gave byte-identical output, crate places after the strike included.

b2.png (board 2, tick 400): a perspective view from front and above of the whole slab. The ball is a red shaded sphere at x~1.1. Two crate pairs sit at x 0 and the pushed pair at x~1.55, all boxes with a lighter top and darker sides, and the 2 coins left show. b3.png: two slabs, the gap and the green bridge at bx 0.44 with the ball and coin on it.

In Spanish, f_title, f_settings, f_paused, f_won and f_lost show Empezar/Ajustes/Salir, Ajustes/Volumen/Idioma/Volver, En pausa/Continuar/Salir al titulo, Ganaste/Puntos: 30, and Fin del juego/Puntos: 10. Play frames show 'Board 2 of 3  Score: 10  Lives: 3' and 'Tablero 2 de 3 Puntos: 0 Vidas: 3'.

The README says nothing about volume scaling the sounds, and lib.rs plays every sound as cx.sound(s, None, 1.0) with no reference to the volume. Only the engine's notes/how.md says the engine scales by volume. 'sounds' does list the sounds at volume 0, but I could not observe the heard gain because run.sounds_heard is not in the report.

The README gives the controls and rules, the three check commands (headless run, frame, sounds), all run by me as written and working, and a Files section mapping game.json, lib.rs, actions.json, ui, strings and sounds.

defects: --set board=N alone leaves the run on the title. The script needs 0:enter first, although the brief says the run starts in play on that board (the README states this).
'selected' reports 'Back_to_title' and 'Quit_to_title' (ids with underscores), not the English words shown.
The title-screen frame shows the red ball floating behind the title panel.

Crates hardly react to impact: a ball at about 4 m/s bounces back off the wall and no crate moves. They only slide under a held push and never topple, so pushing one off an edge is very hard in practice.
'bounce' also plays when the ball rolls level from the first slab onto the bridge (no landing). The ball also gains speed (about 2.0 to 2.5 m/s) when it rolls onto the moving bridge.
The report has an extra 'phase' key that the brief does not ask for (harmless).
could_not_check: m13: none of my input scripts got a crate off the board's edge (the ball always slipped round the crates), so a crate falling and leaving 'crates' was never seen.

m23 (audible part): the report has no heard gain (run.sounds_heard is not a report line), so I could not observe silence at volume 0. The item fails anyway because neither the README nor the code shows the volume scaling.
